parrafos: The term social in regard to media suggests platforms enable communal activity. Social media helps people connect and build networks. Users access social media through web-based or mobile applications. These interactive platforms allow individuals, communities, businesses, and organizations to share, co-create, discuss, participate in, and modify user-generated or self-curated content. Social media is used to share memories, form friendships, build communities and learn. They may be used to promote people, companies, products, and ideas. Social media can be used to consume, publish, or share news.

Popular social media platforms with over 100 million registered users include X, Facebook, WeChat, ShareChat, Instagram, Pinterest, QZone, Weibo, VK, Tumblr, Baidu Tieba, Threads, and LinkedIn. Depending on the interpretation, other popular platforms that are sometimes referred to as social media services include YouTube, Letterboxd, QQ, Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, LINE, Snapchat, Viber, Reddit, Discord, and TikTok. Wikis and Roblox are examples of collaborative content creation.

Social media outlets differ from old media (e.g. newspapers, TV, and radio broadcasting) in many ways, including quality, reach, frequency, usability, relevancy, and permanence. Social media outlets operate in a dialogic transmission system (many sources to many receivers) while traditional media operate under a monologic transmission model (one source to many receivers). For instance, a newspaper is delivered to many subscribers, and a radio station broadcasts the same programs to a city.

Social media has been criticized for a range of negative impacts on children and teenagers, including exposure to inappropriate content, exploitation by adults, sleep problems, attention problems, feelings of exclusion, and various mental health maladies. Social media has also received criticism as worsening political polarization and undermining democracy, exacerbated by platform capture by vested interests, with journalist Maria Ressa deeming it "toxic sludge" for increasing distrust among members of society. During the 2020s, concerns have emerged over the risk posed by the large influence of social media platforms based in the United States to the sovereignty of countries in Europe, South America and Australasia.

Major news outlets across the world often have strong controls in place to avoid and fix false claims, but social media's unique qualities bring viral content with little to no oversight. According to the American Psychological Association, "Algorithms that track user engagement to prioritize what is shown tend to favor content that spurs negative emotions like anger and outrage. Overall, most online misinformation originates from a small minority of "superspreaders," but social media amplifies their reach and influence."

The PLATO system was launched in 1960 at the University of Illinois and subsequently commercially marketed by Control Data Corporation. It offered early forms of social media features with innovations such as Notes, PLATO's message-forum application; TERM-talk, its instant-messaging feature; Talkomatic, perhaps the first online chat room; News Report, a crowdsourced online newspaper, and blog and Access Lists, enabling the owner of a note file or other application to limit access to a certain set of users, for example, only friends, classmates, or co-workers.

ARPANET, which came online in 1969, had by the late 1970s enabled exchange of non-government/business ideas and communication, as evidenced by the network etiquette (or "netiquette") described in a 1982 handbook on computing at MIT's Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. ARPANET evolved into the Internet in the 1990s. Usenet, conceived by Tom Truscott and Jim Ellis in 1979 at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and Duke University, was the first open social media app, established in 1980.

A precursor of the electronic bulletin board system (BBS), known as Community Memory, appeared by 1973. Mainstream BBSs arrived with the Computer Bulletin Board System in Chicago, which launched on February 16, 1978. Before long, most major US cities had more than one BBS, running on TRS-80, Apple II, Atari 8-bit computers, IBM PC, Commodore 64, Sinclair, and others. CompuServe, Prodigy, and AOL were three of the largest BBS companies and were the first to migrate to the Internet in the 1990s. Between the mid-1980s and the mid-1990s, BBSes numbered in the tens of thousands in North America alone. Message forums were the signature BBS phenomenon throughout the 1980s and early 1990s.

In 1991, Tim Berners-Lee integrated HTML hypertext software with the Internet, creating the World Wide Web. This breakthrough led to an explosion of blogs, list servers, and email services. Message forums migrated to the web, and evolved into Internet forums, supported by cheaper access as well as the ability to handle far more people simultaneously.
The evolution of online services progressed from serving as channels for networked communication to becoming interactive platforms for networked social interaction with the advent of Web 2.0.

Social media started in the mid-1990s with the invention of platforms like Classmates.com, and SixDegrees.com. While instant messaging and chat clients existed at the time, SixDegrees was unique as it was the first online service designed for people to connect using their actual names instead of anonymously. It boasted features like profiles, friends lists, and school affiliations, making it "the very first social networking site". The platform's name was inspired by the "six degrees of separation" concept, which suggests that every person on the planet is just six connections away from everyone else.

Research from 2015 reported that globally, users spent 22% of their online time on social networks, likely fueled by the availability of smartphones. As of 2023, as many as 4.76 billion people used social media some 59% of the global population.

In 2019, Merriam-Webster defined social media as "forms of electronic communication (such as websites for social networking and microblogging) through which users create online communities to share information, ideas, personal messages, and other content (such as videos)."

The American National Institute of Standards and Technology defines it as "Forms of electronic communications, including websites and applications, that enable users to create and share content or to participate in social networking."

Mobile social media refers to the use of social media on mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets. It is distinguished by its ubiquity, since users no longer have to be at a desk in order to participate on a computer. Mobile services can use the user's location to offer information, connections, or services relevant to that location.

Certain content, has the potential to spread virally, an analogy for the way viral infections spread contagiously from individual to individual. Viral videos are one example. One user spreads a post across their network, which leads those users to follow suit. A post from a relatively unknown user can reach vast numbers of people within hours. Virality is not guaranteed; few posts make the transition.

Viral marketing campaigns are particularly attractive to businesses because they can achieve widespread advertising coverage at a fraction of the cost of traditional marketing campaigns. Nonprofit organizations and activists may also attempt to spread content virally.
Bots are automated programs that operate on the internet. They automate many communication tasks. This has led to the creation of an industry of bot providers.

Chatbots and social bots are programmed to mimic human interactions such as liking, commenting, and following. Bots have also been developed to facilitate social media marketing. Bots have led the marketing industry into an analytical crisis, as bots make it difficult to differentiate between human interactions and bot interactions. Some bots violate platforms' terms of use, which can result in bans and campaigns to eliminate bots categorically. Bots may even pose as real people to avoid prohibitions.

'Cyborgs'—either bot-assisted humans or human-assisted bots—are used for both legitimate and illegitimate purposes, from spreading fake news to creating marketing buzz. A human writes a post content and the bot posts it a specific time. In other cases, cyborgs spread fake news. Cyborgs may work as sock puppets, where one human pretends to be someone else, or operates multiple accounts, each pretending to be a person.

A multitude of United States patents are related to social media, and their numbers are growing, albeit unevenly. For example, there were 897 patents in Q3 2024 and 1,674 in Q2. And even in Q3, the U.S. share of all social media patent applications was 50% of all patent applications, with second-placed China at 18%. As of 2020, over 5000 social media patent applications had been published in the United States. Only slightly over 100 patents had been issued.

Examples are the social hub site Facebook launching an integrated video platform in May 2007, and Instagram, whose original scope was low-resolution photo sharing, introducing the ability to share quarter-minute 640×640 pixel videos (later extended to a minute with increased resolution). Instagram later implemented stories (short videos self-destructing after 24 hours), a concept popularized by Snapchat, as well as IGTV, for seekable videos. Stories were then adopted by YouTube.
X, whose original scope was text-based microblogging, later adopted photo sharing, then video sharing, then a media studio for business users, after YouTube's Creator Studio.

The discussion platform Reddit added an integrated image hoster replacing the external image sharing platform Imgur, and then an internal video hosting service, followed by image galleries (multiple images in a single post), known from Imgur. Imgur implemented video sharing.
According to Statista, it is estimated that, in 2022, around 3.96 billion people were using social media globally. This number is up from 3.6 billion in 2020.
The following is a list of the most popular social networking services based on the number of active users as of January 2024 per Statista.

A 2009 study suggested that individual differences may help explain who uses social media: extraversion and openness have a positive relationship with social media, while emotional stability has a negative sloping relationship with social media. A 2015 study reported that people with a higher social comparison orientation appear to use social media more heavily than people with low social comparison orientation.
resumen_es: Qué son las redes sociales, en qué se diferencian de los medios tradicionales, de dónde vienen (de PLATO y los BBS a la web 2.0) y qué problemas plantean: efectos en los menores, desinformación, viralidad y bots.
nivel_motivo: Buena parte de las palabras que bajan la cobertura léxica son nombres de plataformas, siglas y marcas; el vocabulario general y la sintaxis corresponden a un B2 alto.

ideas_clave.idea: Social media are web and mobile platforms that let people and organisations create, share and discuss content, build networks, promote ideas and follow the news.
Many platforms have over 100 million users, although which services count as social media depends on the definition used.
Unlike traditional media, which send one message from a single source to many receivers, social media connect many sources with many receivers.

They are criticised for harming young people, deepening polarisation, threatening national sovereignty and spreading misinformation, since engagement-driven algorithms reward content that provokes anger.
Their precursors include PLATO in the 1960s, ARPANET and Usenet, and the bulletin board systems that flourished in North America in the 1980s and early 1990s.
The World Wide Web and later Web 2.0 turned online services into spaces for social interaction, and in the mid-1990s SixDegrees became the first network based on users' real identities.
Smartphones have fuelled use, and by 2023 almost six in ten people worldwide were on social media.
Dictionaries and official bodies define social media as forms of electronic communication through which users create communities and share content.
Mobile social media are available everywhere and can use the user's location to offer relevant services.
Some content spreads virally from user to user, which makes viral campaigns a cheap and attractive tool for businesses and activists, even though success is rare.
Bots and human-bot hybrids automate interactions, distort marketing data and can be used to spread fake news or impersonate real people.
Patent applications related to social media are rising unevenly, led by the United States and followed by China.
Platforms constantly copy each other's features, so services that started with photos or text have added video, stories and image galleries.
The number of users keeps growing, and studies link heavier use to personality traits such as extraversion, openness and a tendency to compare oneself with others.

resumen_modelo: The text presents social media as web and mobile platforms through which individuals and organisations create, share and discuss content, build networks and access news. What distinguishes them from newspapers, radio or television is their dialogic nature: instead of a single source addressing many receivers, many sources communicate with many receivers. However, they have attracted strong criticism, as they are accused of harming children and teenagers, fuelling political polarisation, undermining democracy and even threatening national sovereignty. Moreover, since algorithms prioritise content that arouses anger, they amplify the misinformation produced by a small number of users. Historically, social media grew out of earlier systems such as PLATO, ARPANET, Usenet and the bulletin boards of the 1980s. The creation of the World Wide Web and then Web 2.0 transformed online services into platforms for social interaction, and in the mid-1990s SixDegrees became the first network in which users appeared under their real names. Partly thanks to smartphones, which allow constant and location-based use, around 59% of the world's population was using social media by 2023. The author then turns to some specific phenomena. Content can spread virally, which explains why companies and activists value viral campaigns, although few posts actually succeed. At the same time, bots and “cyborgs” that mimic human behaviour make it difficult to measure genuine engagement and may be used to disseminate fake news. Finally, the text mentions the growing number of patents, the tendency of platforms to imitate each other's features, and studies associating intensive use with certain personality traits.

preguntas.pregunta: Which transmission model do social media outlets follow, according to the text?
opciones: A dialogic model: many sources to many receivers
A monologic model: one source to many receivers
A one-to-one model: one source to one receiver
A centralised model: many sources to one receiver
respuestas: A dialogic model: many sources to many receivers
preguntas.cita: Social media outlets operate in a dialogic transmission system (many sources to many receivers)
preguntas.explicacion: El modelo monológico (una fuente, muchos receptores) es el de los medios tradicionales. Los otros dos modelos no aparecen en el texto.

preguntas.explicacion: «Vested interests» son los intereses creados: grupos que se benefician de una situación y quieren mantenerla.

preguntas.explicacion: La APA dice que la mayor parte de la desinformación procede de una pequeña minoría de «superdifusores», cuyo alcance amplifican las redes.

preguntas.explicacion: Los demás elementos también eran de PLATO, pero corresponden a News Report (periódico colaborativo), Notes (foros) y TERM-talk (mensajería instantánea).

preguntas.pregunta: Users had to pay a monthly fee to access the Computer Bulletin Board System in Chicago.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto da la fecha de lanzamiento de ese sistema, pero no dice nada sobre si era de pago.

preguntas.pregunta: What did Tim Berners-Lee create in 1991?
preguntas.explicacion: Berners-Lee integró el hipertexto HTML con Internet y creó la web. ARPANET es de 1969, los primeros BBS de los años setenta y SixDegrees de mediados de los noventa.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is SixDegrees described as “the very first social networking site”?
respuestas: Because it was the first online service designed for people to connect under their real names rather than anonymously, and it offered features such as profiles, friends lists and school affiliations.
preguntas.cita: it was the first online service designed for people to connect using their actual names instead of anonymously
preguntas.explicacion: La novedad no era la comunicación en línea, que ya existía, sino la identidad real y los perfiles con listas de amigos.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o no se dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: By 2023 more than half of the world's population used social media.
preguntas.cita: 4.76 billion people used social media some 59% of the global population
preguntas.explicacion: El 59 % de la población mundial es más de la mitad, así que la afirmación es verdadera.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 14 una palabra que signifique «omnipresencia».
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning “the fact of being everywhere”.
preguntas.cita: It is distinguished by its ubiquity
preguntas.explicacion: «Ubiquity» es la capacidad de estar en todas partes: con el móvil ya no hace falta estar ante un ordenador.

preguntas.pregunta: Why are viral marketing campaigns particularly attractive to businesses?
opciones: They can reach a wide audience at a fraction of the cost of traditional campaigns
They are guaranteed to reach millions of people
They are not subject to platforms' terms of use
They replace the need for any advertising budget
respuestas: They can reach a wide audience at a fraction of the cost of traditional campaigns
preguntas.cita: they can achieve widespread advertising coverage at a fraction of the cost of traditional marketing campaigns
preguntas.explicacion: La ventaja es el coste reducido. El texto advierte además que la viralidad no está garantizada, y nada dice de que escapen a las normas de las plataformas.

preguntas.pregunta: How have bots affected the marketing industry?
respuestas: They have caused an analytical crisis, because it has become hard to tell genuine human interactions from automated ones, which distorts the measurement of engagement.
preguntas.cita: Bots have led the marketing industry into an analytical crisis
preguntas.explicacion: La clave es la dificultad de distinguir interacciones humanas de las de bots, lo que vuelve poco fiables los datos de marketing.

preguntas.cita: Cyborgs may work as sock puppets
preguntas.explicacion: Un «sock puppet» (literalmente, títere de calcetín) es una identidad falsa en internet; el propio texto lo explica a continuación.

preguntas.pregunta: Which feature did Instagram adopt from a concept popularised by Snapchat?
preguntas.cita: Instagram later implemented stories (short videos self-destructing after 24 hours), a concept popularized by Snapchat
preguntas.explicacion: Las «stories» venían de Snapchat. IGTV fue una creación propia de Instagram, Creator Studio es de YouTube y las galerías de imágenes las adoptó Reddit a partir de Imgur.

preguntas.pregunta: Which personal characteristics are associated with heavier use of social media?
respuestas: Extraversion and openness are positively related to social media use, as is a strong tendency to compare oneself with others, whereas emotional stability is negatively related to it.
preguntas.cita: extraversion and openness have a positive relationship with social media
preguntas.explicacion: El párrafo resume dos estudios: uno de 2009 sobre rasgos de personalidad y otro de 2015 sobre la comparación social.

glosario.nota: «To curate» se usa mucho en inglés digital: seleccionar y organizar contenido.
En otros contextos «outlet» es «punto de venta» o «toma de corriente».
Falso amigo parcial: también puede significar «descuido», según el contexto.
